result.topic_en: Two new methods for determining the biquadratic character ('Decident') of a Gaussian integer m modulo a Gaussian prime M via sums of integer parts, with a worked numerical table for M = -1-6i, m = 3-2i, dated 14 December 1843.

Math 13 [-43-] [-32-]
Neue Methoden zur Best.
des biquadratischen Decidents
(41)
1) $f$ alle geraden zwischen $0 /\!/ 2D$
wofür $\mathrm{Int.}\frac{2f}{M} = 0$
$\Sigma\, \mathrm{Int.}\frac{fm}{M} = \mathrm{Dec.}\frac{m}{M}$

methods.what: First method: biquadratic character of m mod M as the sum of integer parts (Gaussian floor) of fm/M over even f between 0 and 2D with Int(2f/M)=0
Second method: signed sum over integers F between 0 and D/2 with Int(2F/M) even, sign + for F even, - for F odd
Reformulation of the second method as the real part of a sum weighted by powers of i, equal to a sum weighted by (-1)^F
Numerical worked example for M = -1-6i, m = 3-2i (norm 37), tabulating F and the integer parts, giving Dec = -2

items.english: The sum of the integer parts of fm/M equals the decident (biquadratic character) of m with respect to M.
The signed sum of (Int(Fm/M) - Int(F/M)) equals the decident of m with respect to M.
